div.head: Further: the Book of Ezekiel. And in it there are twenty-eight sections.

div.ab: First, the proem. Ezekiel was of the order of the priests. And with Jeconiah he was carried away to Babylon when Nebuchadnezzar came up the third time against Jerusalem. ¹⁰And there he prophesied twenty-eight years, but a leader of the Jews killed him because he had rebuked him for worshipping idols. And he was buried in the grave of Shem and Arpachshad, the sons of Noah, before the return of the people.

div.head: Section First.
div.ab:
(1:1) It came to pass in the thirtieth year, i.e., of the life of Ezekiel himself. In the fifth, i.e., in the fifth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin. In the fourth month, i.e., Tammuz. ¹⁵By the river Kᵉvar, < with stopping of k and fricativeness of b > , i.e., the Euphrates. (1:3) The hand of the Lord, i.e., his visitation. (1:4) A storm wind, i.e., a type of terrifying swiftness of the coming of the Babylonians. And a fire that broke out in flames, i.e., a type of severe punishment, the chariot (represents) the entire world. (1:5) And out of its midst the like
ness of four faces. The lion is a type of all beasts of prey; the bull, a type of all cattle; the eagle, a type of all flying things; ²⁰the man, a type of the microcosm, comprising all created things. And this was their appearance, as the likeness of human beings, i.e., they stood upright and not upon all fours. (1:6) And every one had four faces and four wings, i.e., upon every side a face, and between every two faces a wing. (1:7) And their legs (were) straight, i.e., like a man's and not curved like those of irrational beasts. And ²⁵the hoofs of their feet (were) like calves' hoofs, i.e., firm. And flashing like copper which flashes, a type of the splendor of divine grace which is spread over everything. (1:8) And the hand of a man under their wings, i.e., a type of the divine will, upon which everything depends. (1:9) And when they went [they went] straight forward and did not turn, i.e., because on all sides their gaze was straight-forward they did not need ³⁰to turn about. (1:14) As the appear
ance of lightning, i.e., glinting. (1:15) And, behold, a wheel upon the earth, i.e., a type of swiftness of revolution. (1:16) As the appearance of a tarshish, i.e., a stone fiery in color. As a wheel in the midst of a wheel, i.e., that their rotation might be with ease. (1:17) And to the place whither their front was turned < with å of sh > to go, they went, i.e., to the likeness of a human being which was lifted up they adhered closely. (1:18) And their ³⁵upper arcs were high and they were conspicuous < with a of ḥ > , i.e., a type of the encompassing heaven. And their upper arc was full of eyes, i.e., a type of the stars. (1:22) Crystal, i.e., white beryl. (1:24) And like the voice of God, i.e., the sound of their wings was fearful. They let hang down, < with a of m > . (1:26) And......the canopy is the chariot itself. A sapphire, i.e., the color of heaven. And upon the likeness
of the throne........something like the appearance of a human being was upon the top of it, i.e., a type of Immanuel. (1:28) As the appearance of the bow that is in the clouds, i.e., a type of the variety of operations of the divine government. But in another manner (of interpretation) the things of the chariot bear a type of the things pertaining to our Lord.
The four animals are the four Evangelists. ⁵The lion is a type of the courage of the apostles, and the eagle is a type of their solicitude for mankind. The bull is a type of their cultivation of the soil of the hearts by the [seed] of life-giving teachings. And the man is their rational nature; the charioteer is the Messiah. The hurricane wind (represents) the spread of the Gospel. The wheel in the midst of a wheel is a type of the New Covenant which was bound up in the bosom of the Old. And the eyes that were in all of their body are a type of fullness ¹⁰of knowledge. And the hand of a man under their wings, i.e., the divine power which attended them. But Dionysius presents these things more mystically, for he understands the lion (to be) a symbol of the strength and the hiding of the traces of the angelic natures; and the bull, a type of the refreshing of the furrows for (the reception of) spiritual rains; and the eagle, a type of the majesty and swiftness of flight and vision that belongs to them. (2:1) And he said to me, ¹⁵O human being, stand up on thy feet; I will speak with thee, i.e., indicating the humility of him who would not boast of the amazing revelation he had been esteemed worthy to see. (2:6) Because
thou art dwelling among scorpions, i.e., and offspring also of vipers, as John the Baptist called them. (2:8) Be not thou rebellious, i.e., do not draw back from anything that I tell thee. (2:10) And written before and ²⁰behind,i.e., a type of the multitude of exhortations. And there were written in it wailings and lamentations and mourning, i.e., the account of the trials that were approaching. (3:2) And he caused me to eat that roll, i.e., it was spiritual, however, and not material. (3:6) Their speech, < with a of l > . (3:7) Hard of forehead, i.e., headstrong. (3:9) As adamant that is harder than flint have I made thy forehead, i.e., I have set thee in authority over them. (3:14) And the Spirit lifted me up ²⁵and carried me away, i.e., in spirit and it was not in body, (3:15) to Tel'åkhīv.

div.head: Section Second.
div.ab:
(3:22) Arise, go out to the plain, i.e., get away from worldly affairs. (3:24) Go, shut thyself within thy house, i.e., until the time for speaking. (4:1,2) Take thee a brick..... and engrave upon it.....Jerusalem, and set against it a siege......... and...... ramparts and.....ambushes, i.e., in thought. (4:3) And thou, take thee a griddle of iron and make it a ³⁰wall, i.e., a symbol that, even though of iron, the wall
of Jerusalem would be pierced. And set thy face against it, i.e., in wrath. (4:4) And thou, lie down upon thy side, i.e., a type of the duration of the trial, and the left hand Israel, the right hand those of the house of Judah. And place the iniquity of the house of Israel upon it, i.e., punishment, (4:5) Three hundred and ninety days. (4:6) And thou shalt lie on thy right side and thou shalt bear ³⁵the iniquity of the house of Judah forty days, a day for a year have I given thee, i.e., a type of the greatness of the iniquity of the house of Israel, and the smallness of the iniquity of the house of Judah, and so four hundred and thirty years God bore the iniquity of both of them, and after that he delivered them to a complete captivity. For from the fourth year of Solomon when he began to build the temple and until the eleventh year
of Zedekiah when it was burned is the approximate sum total of this number, because the years that Amon reigned are reckoned as two according to the book of Kings and not twelve according to the Chronicle. (4:8) Behold, I have placed chains upon thee, and thou shalt not turn thyself from one side to the other, i.e., a symbol of the unchangeableness of his affliction. (4:9)And take thee grains of wheat ⁵and barley, i.e., all these
represented various types of their rebellion. (5:1) Take thee a sharp sword like a barber's razor and pass it over thy head and over thy beard, i.e., a type of the abolition of the kingdom and the priesthood by the sword of the Babylonian. And divide them into three parts, i.e., the hair of the head and of the beard. And the part that is burned is a type of those who die in the midst of the city, and (the part) that is cut to pieces by the sword a type of those ¹⁰who are killed, and (the part) that is scattered in the wind (cf. 5:2) a type of those who are dispersed throughout the countries. (5:3) And thou shalt bind them up in thy skirt, i.e., a type of the redeemed who will dwell in Jerusalem.

div.head: Section Third.
div.ab:
(6:6) And the shrines shall be desolate, i.e., the little houses for the idols, < feminine gender >. (6:11) Smite with thy palm and stamp with thy foot, i.e., a type of the exultation of the Gentiles over the destruction of the Hebrews. (7:7) And the goat is coming, i.e., the Babylonian, who leaps like a kid. O, inhabitant of the land, i.e., the great ruler. (7:10) And ¹⁵the rod hath blossomed, i.e., (the rod) of the Babylonian. (7:11) Against the rod of wickedness, i.e., Judah. Not by them nor by their agitation nor by their action, i.e., of the house of Judah; they will not be helped by themselves, nor by their worship of idols, nor by their shameful deeds.
(7:13) For the vision will not be turned back concerning all their possessions, i.e., the prophecy concerning their complete destruction is not to be considered deceptive. (7:22) And they shall pass among the bricks, i.e., they will destroy the buildings. (8:3) And he seized me by the locks of my head and the Spirit transported me between the earth and the heaven, ²⁰and brought me to Jerusalem, i.e., in spirit. And there stood the statue of zeal, i.e., the idol of wrath.

div.head: Section Fourth.
div.ab:
(8:11) Azaniah, the son of Shaphan, i.e., who was a priest of the demons. (8:14) And I saw there women as they were sitting and weeping for Tammuz, i.e., Tammuz is the same as Ares. And the pagans foolishly say in their fables that he was a shepherd, and Belati, the daughter of Hercules, the king of Cyprus, loved him. And after he took her and ²⁵fled to Mount Lebanon, there a wild boar ripped him open and he died, and, moreover, because of the strength of her passion she fell upon his body and died. But the gods, because they had pity on them, placed them in heaven, and the pagans every year observe a feast of lamentation for them. And so also the Hebrews did, imitating them. (8:17) And they snort with their nostrils, i.e., they burn with anger and blaspheme. (9:1) Draw near, ye avengers ³⁰of the city, i.e., the (divine) will commanded the angels. (9:2) And I saw six men, i.e., a type of the
might of the Babylonian. And the altar of copper is a type of the abolition of the priesthood and the sacrifices. (9:4) And trace a mark upon their foreheads, i.e., that the good might be separated from the evil. (9:7) Defile......the ruined courts,<masculine gender> . (10:2) Go in between the wheels, i.e., a type of the immanence of the wrath. (10:9) Four wheels,<with l [after l]> . (10:13) And ʾelūpnē he ³⁵called them <with vowellessness of the Greek p> , i.e., hurried and swift. (10:14) One the face of a cherub, i.e., instead of the face of a bull he put here the face of a cherub. And, perhaps, the bull was a type of their priesthood, which had ceased.

div.head: Section Fifth.
div.ab:
(11:3) It is the caldron and we the flesh, i.e., we shall not go out of it though we be boiled in it like flesh in a pot of copper. (11:13) Pelatiah,
the son of Banja. (11:16) A little sanctuary, i.e., [in] a congregation that is smaller than that in Jerusalem they shall sanctify me. (12:3) And make thyself a captive, i.e., a type of their captivity. (12:5) And break through the wall, i.e., a type of the destruction of Jerusalem. (12:13) To the land of the Chaldeans, yet he shall not see it, i.e., they
will put out his eyes. (12:22) Speaking in proverbs.... and saying, The days are prolonged and ⁵every vision fails, i.e., it will not be fulfilled in our days.

div.head: Section Sixth.
div.ab: (13:4) Like foxes in the waste places are thy prophets, O Israel, i.e., they speak craftily. (13:10) And he was building a wall, i.e., the Lord, for the people. And they were plastering it so that it would fall, i.e., the false prophets who encouraged the people and did not permit them to repent. (13:11) And stones of great hardness shall fall, i.e., of hail, a type of the Babylonians. (13:18) Woe to those that sew pillows for the elbows, i.e., that they might lean on them and live luxuriously. (13:19) ¹⁰And ye have profaned my people for handfuls of barley and for pieces of bread, i.e., with the like of these things they work enchantments. (14:9) I the Lord have led that prophet astray, i.e., I turned him from his uprightness. (14:14) And if there were in it these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, i.e., not even those whom I heard and delivered from great trials when they prayed unto me would I answer if they should pray for this people. And ¹⁵Job he put after Daniel, either because the learned had doubts as to whether his history was literally true or not, or because salvation from the flood and deliverance from the mouth of lions were more marvelous than recovery from a plague.

div.head: Section Seventh.
div.ab:
(15:2) What belongs to the
vine-tree more than any tree? i.e., if it does not produce grapes it is fit for the fire only, so also the children of Israel. (15:4) And both its ends, ²⁰i.e., Israel and Judah. (16:3) Thine origin and thy birth is from the land of Canaan, thy father was an Amorite and thy mother a Hittite, i.e., you have imitated them in your deeds. (16:4) And she that delivered thee on the day of thy birth <with a of l> , i.e., the midwife, in the day when she delivered thee from thy mother when thou wast born, she did not cut thy navel-string, i.e., she was not concerned about thy good development. (16:6) In thy blood live, i.e., in thy defilement. (16:7) Thy breasts ²⁵have developed and thy hair grown, i.e., thou hast advanced in deadly practices. And thou wast naked and bare, [i.e.,] of grace. (16:8) And I saw thy time was the time of the medlar plant, i.e., whose berry is the most despised of fruits, and full of stones. (16:10) Embroidered work, interwoven of linen and wool, and the priests and women alone wore it. And I covered thee with a veil <with e of ḥ>, i.e., thin white stuff which women place over their ³⁰faces and see and are not seen. (16:13) Gems, (ḥᵉmūrtå), i.e., a precious stone much used for beads. (16:15) And thou didst play the
harlot because of thy renown, i.e., thou wast reputed and renowned in fornication. (16:16) And thou didst make thee images <with å of n> , i.e., idols which they sewed out of cloth. (16:24) Thou didst build thee vaulted rooms<with a of g and vowellessness of l and fricativeness of b> , i.e., large idol houses. (16:25) And shrines, i.e., little houses. (16:26) And thou didst commit fornication with ³⁵the Egyptians, thy neighbors, the great of flesh, i.e., the mighty ones in heathendom. (16:27) And I will destroy thine ordinances, i.e., the laws which Jeroboam the son of Nebat and the rest gave you. (16:33) And thou didst corrupt them with thy fornication, i.e., thou didst bring offerings to the idols with whom thou didst commit fornication.

div.head: Section Eighth.
div.ab:
(16:45) Thou art the daughter of thy mother who forsook her husband and her children, i.e., her mother was the congregation that made the calf in the wilderness, and her husband was God, and her sons Moses and Aaron
and the rest of the virtuous. (16:46) Sodom and her daughters, i.e., her towns. (16:55) And thy sister Sodom and her daughters shall be constituted as of yore, i.e., thy constitution shall be like Sodom's (17:2) Put forth a riddle and speak a parable, i.e., that seeing they shall not see, as our Lord has said.
(17:3) A great eagle, i.e., Nebuchadnezzar. Thickly feathered <with e of m ⁵and g stopped> came to Lebanon, i.e., to Judah that was rich in men as Lebanon is in trees. And took of the choicest of the junipers, i.e., the evergreen box, a type of the sons of the kings who were of the seed of David. (17:4) And he cut off the head of its growth, i.e., he lopped off, and took away the highest part of it , a type of Jeconiah. Growth, i.e., the crown (?). A city of merchants, i.e., Babylon. (17:5) And he set (it) in the wilderness, i.e., in Jerusalem, which was desolate. (17:6) ¹⁰A sickly vine of stunted growth, i.e., Zedekiah. (17:7)And behold another great eagle, i.e., and there was. (17:8) And planted by many waters, i.e., a type of his support by the Babylonians.

div.head: Section Ninth.
div.ab:
(17:22) I will take of the choicest of the high junipers, i.e., of the seed of the kings. From its top I will cut off the best part, i.e., the shoot Zerubbabel, who was from the best part of the highest juniper, David. I will lop off the shoot and plant it in Zion. (17:24) I have laid its high tree low, i.e., Zedekiah. ¹⁵And I have exalted the low tree, i.e., Zerubbabel. (18:6) And upon the mountains he has not eaten, i.e., to the idols he did not sacrifice. (18:7) And he has caused no man to suffer, <with fricativeness of k> ,
from tūkhå. And he hath restored the pledge,<with a of p > . (18:23) I have no pleasure in the death of the sinner,......but that he turn from his evil way and live, i.e., in this I have pleasure. (19:2) What is thy mother, thou lion's whelp? i.e., wherefore, since thy mother, which is the congregation, brought thee up, O thou lion's whelp, Jehoahaz. ²⁰Thou hast become a lion and hast learned crushing and thou hast eaten human beings, that is to say, thou didst become an unjust king, and Pharaoh bound thee and took thee to Egypt. Who is couched among lions, i.e., the other kingdoms. (19:9) And they shut him up in a cage, i.e., they placed Zedekiah in a lion's cage and took him down to Babylon. (19:10) Thy mother is like a vine, in thy blood, planted by the waters, i.e., after thine enemies have shed thy blood, O Israel, again ²⁵thou shalt possess Jerusalem, thy mother. (19:14) And a fire has gone out from its choice rods and has eaten up its fruit, i.e., injustice came forth from her kings and destroyed her sons. This is a lamentation and shall be for a lamentation, i.e., I spoke this word mourning, and so the people, when they mourn, will speak it.

div.head: Section Tenth.
div.ab:
(20:25) And I gave them statutes that were not pleasing and ordinances wherein they would not live, i.e., he called the Ten Commandments statutes
³⁰and ordinances which, if a man do them, he lives, and the sacrifices (were) the statutes which were not pleasing. Because for a man not to sin and not to sacrifice is even better before God than to sin and to sacrifice. (20:29) What are the shrines?,<feminine gender> . (20:37) And I will bring you under the discipline of the covenant, i.e., I will chastise you because you have not kept the covenant of my statutes.

div.head: Section Eleventh.
div.ab:
(20:46) And prophesy ³⁵against the [thicket] that is in the South, i.e., against Mount Zion, for it was called South from Babylon, because Babylon was nearer the Eastern Persians and the Northern Huns, but according to the geometric canon ancient Babylon, in which this prophet prophesied, is but thirty-two degrees from the equator, which is in the Southern portion of the habitable earch,
and Jerusalem thirty-three degrees north. (20:47) And it shall devour......thy trees, the green and the dry, i.e., the rich and the poor. (21:2) And look upon their sanctuary, i.e., he does not say my sanctuary, because it had been alienated from them. (21:4) My sword shall go forth, i.e., my vengeance, from its sheath <with fricativeness of t> , i.e., out of my longsuffering. (21:3) And I will cut off from thee ⁵the righteous and the sinner, i.e., not the truly righteous but him who is
righteous in his own sight. (21:9f) A sword, a sword, sharpen and prepare.....to shake violently, i.e, to cause to tremble. But some say it is to tear to pieces, and the scribes by error changed it. The stock of my son, i.e., the provoking son, Israel. (21:13)And though the stock is rejected it shall not be, i.e., it would not be rejected forever, but it would be visited after seventy years. (21:14) ¹⁰And the sword shall be doubled, [i.e.,] it will turn hither and thither. And the third sword is that of the slain, i.e., the first and the second captivity, counting that in the days of Jehoiakim as the first and that in the days of Jeconiah as the second, and the complete captivity which was in the days of Zedekiah as the third. And a prince calls to God, (21:16) Hold fast on my right hand and hold fast on my left hand to the place whither my face is turned, i.e., to Jerusalem, which he ravaged. (21:19) And the chosen hand, i.e., the right. (21:21) ¹⁵He cast the arrow and enquired of his idol, i.e., that it might show him which way he should go up in order to conquer. And when he threw the arrow directly upward, it inclined toward Jerusalem. He beheld his glory, i.e., it was revealed to him in the divination that he would be victorious in battle. (21:23) But it shall be for them as
a vain augury before their eyes, i.e., the Jews, because Nebuchadnezzar was longsuffering toward them, thought that his oracle had deceived him and that he was ²⁰unable to subdue them. (21:26) He exalted the lowly, i.e., Jeconiah, whom Evil-merodach removed from prison. And abased the lofty, i.e., Zedekiah. (21:27) Until he come to whom the rule belongs, i.e., literally Zerubbabel, but spiritually our Lord. (21:30) Assemble in thy strength in the place where thou wast born, i.e., God speaks to the Babylonian. And there I will judge thee, i.e., by means of the Persian. (22:10) And in thee they have uncovered the father's nakedness, i.e., ²⁵a man had commerce with his father's wife. (22:12) And in thee they have exacted too much, i.e., unlawfully. (22:16) And I will make thee quake in the sight of the nations,<with a of , from rᵉthīthå> .

div.head: Section Twelfth.
div.ab:
(22:18) To me....are contemptible....like copper and tin, i.e., when silver is adulterated with them and they enter the furnace they are consumed and the tried silver remains. (22:20) I will melt you,<with a of p>. (23:3) There they pressed their
breasts and there they were deflowered, i.e., in Egypt. Ohola and Oholibah, ³⁰a type of Samaria and Jerusalem. (cf. 23:4). And Samaria the royal city of the ten tribes of Israel he called the elder because she first worshipped the image of four faces that Manasseh made, and Jerusalem the royal city of Judah afterwards. (23:15) And girded with girdles, <with a of m> . (23:20)And she adhered unto their slaves, i.e., the Egyptians who were brought under subjection to the Assyrians. And their genital organs are as the genital organs of horses, ³⁵i.e., ḥanå is predicated of the members of procreation of males and females, in common. (23:22) Whom thy soul has come to loathe <with e of n>, i.e., it has come to abhor. (23:21) And I visited upon thee the evil of thy youth, (170 b) i.e., I visited thee because of thy evil way when in Egypt. (23:33f) The cup of thy sister Samaria thou shalt drink and drain, <with e of t>.

div.head: Section Thirteenth.
div.ab:
(23:39) He entered my sanctuary, <with a of d, but some pronounce q with a and d vowelless> . (23:45) And righteous men shall judge them, i.e., the prophets. (24:3) Set on the caldron, i.e., Jerusalem, which was to be seethed in the fire ⁵of the Babylonians. (24:4) And cast the good and fat pieces into it, i.e., the choicest of the people. The shoulder, the bone of which has been torn out, a type of the king. (24:6) And the lot has not fallen
upon it, i.e., some shall not be delivered and some perish, but all of them shall perish together. (24:11) And its copper shall be melted <with a of p> , i.e., he will destroy its buildings. And her punishment shall be complete, (24:12) like diseased figs, i.e, those that fall and perish. (24:13) Because thou wast made clean ¹⁰and hast not become clean thyself,......thou shalt not be cleansed again, i.e., they taught thee and thou didst not learn, thou shalt not learn again. (24:16) behold, I take away from thee the desire of thine eyes, i.e., I will cause thy wife to die. (24:17) But be grieved in the blood of the dead, i.e., with grief that is hidden in the heart like the blood in the body. And do not put a covering upon thy lips, i.e., thou shalt not be silent. (25:3) Because you said Aha against my sanctuary that was profaned, i.e., you rejoiced.

div.head: Section Fourteenth.
div.ab:
(25:9) Behold, I will shake violently the shoulder of Moab, i.e., I will cause his power to tremble. (25:12) And he has maintained ill-will, i.e., he nursed rancor. (26:2) Because Tyre has said against Jerusalem Aha, i.e, she rejoiced over her calamity. The gates of the peoples are borken, i.e., Jerusalem. And they have returned unto me, i.e, Tyre calls the merchants to herself. (26:4) As a bare rock, i.e., there would not be a building on it. (26:5) And she shall be a place of (nets) spread out,<²⁰with a of t>.
(26:6) And her daughters in the field, i.e., her villages. (27:2) But thou. O human being. lament a lamenta[illegible] may make for thee supports<with å of t and vowellessness of d>, i.e., beams, that is to say, timbers upon which ships are built. (27:6)Of the Kittites, i.e., of the Macedonians. (27:7) That it may be to thee for a sign, i.e., of glory. ʾEles, (27:8) ʾArwadh, (27:10) The Lūdhites, the Pūtites. (27:13) Jawan, Tūvēl, i.e., the Bithynians. Måshåkh, i.e., ²⁵Mysia. In the persons of men, i.e., in male and female slaves.

div.head: Section Fifteenth.
div.ab:
(27:16) Pethkå is cloth woven of wool and linen; pᵉthawtᵉkhå is gold brocade; the shīråyē are purple (cloths). (27:17) The resins are gums of trees; wheat and rice, <with u of r>. (27:15) The sons of Daran, i.e., the sons of Keturah, that is, the Turks. (27:22) Sheba, Raʿma. (27:23) Kanå (or Canneh), ʿAdhan, thy sailors (cf. 27:28). (27:26) Oarsmen, <with i of l without i> . A sultry wind ³⁰has broken thee, i.e., drowned thee in the sea when thou didst flee from the Babylonians. (28:2) Say to the prince of Tyre,.....because thy heart was lifted up and thou saidst I am God, i.e, Hiram, who lived to
a very advanced age, that is to say, all the days of the twenty-two kings of Judah, and their years were 485, thought within himself that he was immortal. But Nebuchadnezzar, after the final captivity of Jerusalem, made war
against Tyre, and they built a bridge of stones in the sea unto her, but when the men of Tyre saw this they threw everything in the sea and fled in ships. But he captured Hiram and killed him. (28:12,13) Thou art the seal of the figure that is full of wisdom and thou wast the crown....in Eden, the Paradise of God, i.e., in this world, and because thou didst not appreciate ⁵the goodness of God, I will destroy thee. In the house of thy stores, i.e., in thy storehouses. From the day that thou wast created, i.e., when thou didst begin to love my people. (28:14) And thou wast with the anointed and overshadowing cherub, i.e., David, whose prayers overshadowed the people. And I set thee in the holy mountain of God, i.e., I deemed thee worthy that thou shouldst have a part in building the temple which Solomon built. And thou wast in the midst of the stones of fire, i.e., in the vicinity ¹⁰of the zealous prophets. (28:16) And I will destroy thee, O thou cherub that overshadows, i.e., Nebuchadnezzar, for he was sent of God. (28:18) Thou
hast profaned thy sanctuary, i.e., thy soul. I will bring forth fire from the midst of thee and it shall consume thee, i.e., thy sin will consume thee. And all these words refer, spiritually, to the Adversary who was overthrown. (28:24) And no more shall there come bitter sorrows<feminine gender> to the house of Israel.

div.head: Section Sixteenth.
div.ab: (29:10) From the tower of Sunå, i.e., the name of him ¹⁵who built it. (29:18) In every head baldness, i.e., of the Babylonians, because of the rocks that were hurled upon them from the wall of Tyre. And every shoulder girded, i.e., for battle. And no wages were given to him or to his army, i.e., because the Tyrians cast all their possessions into the sea, and the Babylonians did not obtain anything from them, but for the service which he rendered against Tyre Egypt was given him as wages. (29:21) And I will open thy mouth, i.e., O, prophet. (30:9) ²⁰Angels shall go forth, i.e., that govern the Babylonians. The city of Sin was the one built in honor of the idol which was fashioned in the form of the moon (cf. 30:15). (30:21) And salve shall not be placed upon it, i.e., he shall have no helper.

div.head: Section Seventeenth.
div.ab:
(31:2) Thou art like, <with a of m> . (31:3) Behold, the Assyrian was a cedar
of Lebanon, i.e., if the Assyrian - so tall - was no match for the Babylonian Nebuchadnezzar, how, O Pharaoh, wilt thou equal his might? (31:8) The ²⁵cedars in the paradise of God did not overtop him, i.e., the kings of the earth did not tower above him. (31:15) In the day when he went down to Sheol I made a mourning, i.e., in the day when the Assyrian perished I made mourning for his people. And all the trees of the field fainted, i.e., the kings of the earth when they heard what had happened were cast down and trembled. (31:18) Thou shalt lie down among the uncircumcised, i.e., because the Egyptian kings had learned from Joseph to circumcise themselves. (32:7) And ³⁰with thy extinction I will cover the heavens, i.e., the air with thy ashes. (32:20) And they shall drag him away, i.e., they shall toss him about violently. (32:21) And the uncircumcised shall lie down, i.e., the peoples who came to the help of the Egyptian. (32:23) In the land of the living, i.e., of promise.

div.head: Section Eighteenth.
div.ab:
(32:26) Måshåkh and Tūvēl, i.e., they were of the house of Gog, who came to the help of the Egyptian. (32:27) And they placed their swords under their heads, i.e., a type of their weakness. And their iniquity was upon their bones, i.e., in their own persons ³⁵they received their retribution. (33:12) The righteousness of the righteous will not deliver him in the day
when he sins, i.e., righteousness and sin are opposites,
they cancel each other. (33:25) Ye eat with the blood, i.e., before the idols. (33:26) Ye stand upon your swords, i.e., ye are persevering in oppression.

div.head: Section Nineteenth.
div.ab: (34:12) As the shepherd seeks out his flock in the day of storm so will I seek out my sheep, i.e., in the day of violent wind. (34:23) ⁵David my servant, he shall shepherd them, i.e., Zerubbabel. (35:6) The blood thou hast hated even that blood shall follow thee, i.e., he says to the children of Edom, that is to say, Esau, since you are blood relations of Israel and hated him it shall pursue you.

div.head: Section Twentieth.
div.ab: (36:13) Because they say unto thee thou art a devourer of men and a bereaver of its people, i.e., other peoples scorned the land of promise because, ¹⁰the sword never ceased from it (cf. II Sam. 12:10), and therefore God promises that he will cause their reproaches to cease from it.

div.head: Section Twenty-first.
div.ab:
(37:1) And the hand of the Lord was upon me, i.e., he visited me through his Holy Spirit. And he set me in a broad valley and it was full of bones, i.e., by the eye of the spirit the prophet saw this vision. To reprimand the Hebrews who did not believe that they should return again to Jerusalem, because of this, to wit, ¹⁵if the soul could return to dry
skeletons, how could it be impossible for it to return to those weary of Babylon? But some say these are the bones of the six hundred thousand who made the exodus from Egypt. (37:9) Come, O wind, from the four winds, i.e., he calls the spirit from the four quarters of the world. Not because they are scattered throughout the world, for the spirits of the righteous dwell in paradise, and the spirits of the wicked in the land of Nod until the resurrection, but because ²⁰their angels have control over the administration of this world. (37:16) Take thee one stick of wood, i.e., here he indicates the union of the two kingdoms after the return. And write upon it Joseph, on the stick of Ephraim, i.e., because the tribe of Ephraim had disappeared, he associated it with his father, Joseph. (38:2) Set thy face toward Gog and the land of Magog, i.e., they were the Scythians, the sons of Japheth, ²⁵and after the return of the people from Babylon when Zerubbabel stood at the head they came up against them and were defeated.

div.head: Section Twenty-second.
div.ab:
(39:9) And they shall burn of them in the fire seven years, [i.e., with their arrows and lances they shall cook the sacrifices in
the temple seven years] . (39:15) He shall set up a pile of stones at the place <with e of n and g>, he would heap up stones as a sign, and the bones of the house of Gog they buried in one place, that the land might not be polluted by them.

div.head: Section Twenty-third.
div.ab: (40:3) A man, and his appearance was as the appearance of copper, ³⁰i.e., the angel Michael, guardian of the people. (40:5) A handbreadth, i.e., (the width of) four fingers when clenched. (40:16)The planks, i.e., the girders upon the pillars. (40:45) This exhedra which looks toward the south, i.e., a mastaba or pillar.

div.head: Section Twenty-fourth.
div.ab: (41:6)And separated from the wall, <with a of m>. (41:7) That the house might be spacious, <with e of n>. (41:12) And the building before the separate place, i.e., the open space. (41:23) And two doors each to the lᵉmarvåvå, i.e., to the square frame. (42:20) ³⁵That he might separate the holy from the common, i.e., the profane.

div.head: Section Twenty-fifth.
div.ab:
(43:15) And the hᵉdhåʾēl
four cubits, i.e., the lectern
upon which the Holy Scriptures were placed, and according to others the altar. (44:2) This door shall be kept shut and shall not be opened, and no man shall enter [by it, i.e., spiritually a type of the Virgin, the mother of Immanuel, the ruler of Israel. (44:9) No alien who is uncircumcised in heart and flesh shall enter] my sanctuary, i.e., clearly showing that circumcision of the flesh alone is unprofitable.

div.head: Section Twenty-sixth.
div.ab:
(44:15) And the priests and the Levites, the sons of Zadok, i.e., who had served as priest ⁵in the days of David, and whose sons did not go astray after idols. (44:20) They shall not allow their locks to grow long, but they shall surely shear their heads, i.e., as also our priests do at present. (44:22) Or a widow who is left a widow by a priest they may take to wife, i.e., the fathers did not permit this rule among the priests in the church of the Christians. (44:24) In all my appointed feasts, i.e., of my festivals. (44:30) And the first of your lumps of dough give to the priests, i.e., ¹⁰the first loaf of bread that you make from the dough of your kneading-troughs. The shekel shall be twenty-five farthings (cf. 45:12) <fem
inine gender> , i.e., zūzē. (45:14) And oil, (a quantity) of ten measures, <with a of j and l>. (45:17) And (the responsibility of) the princes shall be for whole burnt offerings, i.e., of the order of priests, and kings, because they intermingled and intermarried one with the other.

div.head: Section Twenty-seventh.
div.ab:
(46:14) To mix with the fine flour, <with vowellessness of m and a of p> . (46:22) Small courts,¹⁵<feminine gender>. (46:24) That is, the kitchens in which the sacrifices are boiled, i.e., this noun in the Syriac tongue belongs only to the place in which the meat is cooked. (47:1) And I saw waters going forth from under the eastern threshold, i.e., a type of the life-giving teaching of our Lord, who is worshipped toward the east by us: Whoever[#n61-*] is thirsty, let him come to me. (47:3) And when the man had gone forth, glorious, i.e., it was the Lord. ²⁰And the fact that he measured three times the torrent whose water increased from the ankles to the knees, to the loins is a type of the gradual growth of the Gospel. And (47:7) the trees
are a type of the apostles and fathers. (47:8) These waters that go forth toward Galilee, i.e., the place where the apostles were chosen. And they shall fall into the sea among the stinking waters and the waters shall be sweetened, i.e., a type of the abounding heathendom which believed in the life-giving Gospel. (47:10) ²⁵It shall be (a place for) spreading of nets, i.e., a type of the Gentiles that shall be netted by the disciples and teachers of the truth. (47:11) But its outlets and inlets shall not be sweetened, i.e., a type of the Jews among whom first dwelt the heralds of the Gospel, and who were not sweetened by their teaching. (47:12) Every tree of food, i.e., a type of the teachers. And their leaves shall not wither, i.e., they shall not turn back to false doctrines. ³⁰They shall bear early fruit, i.e., they were to bring of the first fruits of their produce and the best of their works.

div.head: Section Twenty-eighth.
div.ab:
(47:13) And of Joseph by line, i.e., a portion shall be given to him in the land. (47:15) Ḥethrūn, Ṣᵉdhadh, (47:16) and Hamath, and Berūth, Hauran, (47:17) Ḥåṣår ʿAjnån, (47:16) and Sᵉpharwīm, (47:17) and Ṣephjūn, (47:19) Tåmår, the waters of Meri
both-Kadesh, (47:20) Nᵉkhåḥ. (48:19) And whoever serves the city shall be served by all the families of Israel, ³⁵i.e., the most solicitous for its building. (48:35) And as for the name of the city, since its (ancient) days the Lord has named it, i.e., Jerusalem, for it is translated light and peace, because it is the city of priesthood and royalty.
The End of the Book of Ezekiel.

p. 34, n. b Cf. LS 72.7f. and see Nöldeke's Grammar, par., 150. This is the regular form for indicating the day of the month.
p. 34, n. c He seems to think of the entire chapter as the description of a chariot.

p. 35, n. c That is, a front or face side.

p. 42, n. c Or synagogue.

p. 47, n. a Cf. verses 3, 4.

p. 50, n. a Mg. adds, And I will reprove thee in the sight of the nations. This is makhsānūthå (reproof) and not rᵉthīthå, which is trembling.
p. 50, n. b A noun formation connected with this root is used in the sense of dross.
p. 50, n. c See collation.
p. 53, n. a Peshitto has Elishah in Gen. 10:4 and I Chron. 1:7, but not here.
p. 53, n. b Some costly embroidered or dyed stuff, difficult to identify exactly.
p. 53, n. c Understood by the Syrians to mean silks.
p. 54, n. a See collation.
p. 55, n. a Possibly thyself.
p. 57, n. a Literally upon.
p. 58, n. a The Semites generally used the same words to indicate wind, breath, soul, and spirit.
p. 58, n. b The reference is to Judith and Holofernes; Holofernes is equated with Magog. BCS, p.33,ll.2,3; Lat. trans. p. 31. Cf. CMS, p. 64, col. 1, ll. 64-67.
p. 58, n. c Added from mss. 2, 14, 20.
p. 59, n. a Literally, bridges.
p. 59, n. b An inner Syriac corruption of a lexicographical note. The Greek στόα should probably be substituted for the Persian sutūn. BS has στόα.
p. 59, n. c The Syrians themselves were uncertain about this word. Cf. BB, col. 1149f., col. 1639f. It is most often conceived of as a door or doors within a door.
p. 59, n. d A corruption of the MT harel.
p. 60, n. a All mss. except 1.

p. 61, n. a The term translated kitchens.
p. 61, n. b The direction toward which many Christians face when they pray and toward which their churches are often oriented.

p. 61, n. c This is the name which the angel who appeared to Manoah the father of Samson bears in the Syriac (Judges 13:18), and it may here be a proper name. It may, however, be a participle passive,being glorified, or active,giving praise.
p. 62, n. a So apparently P with Septuagint.
p. 62, n. b Cf. Mk. 1:17 and parallel passages.
p. 63, n. a The reference is probably to the Urim and Thummin.
